view.lede: The Hill Track, right-handed: one of the five generic courses that every course without its own build races on for now (stiff, uphill finish), with the bigger of its two stand sides. A pear-shaped course of about 1m5f, wide at the stands end and narrow at the far end: a tight downhill turn into a 3½f run-in that climbs all the way to the post, and a stiff 6f sprint course uphill from start to finish. Dressed as a hill course, the bigger stand side.
notes: Beverley, Carlisle, Hamilton, Pontefract, Bath, Chepstow (undulating).
About 13.6f round, a 3.55f run-in. Drawn from a few numbers (the corners and bends of the loop, the chutes), so it can be reshaped quickly.
Hill course, the bigger stand side: old small stands and pavilions clustered round the winning post, near the end of the straight, the crowd up to the rail, the festival in the infield opposite.
Choose Medium or Low under Quality in the race view's bar. Auto steps down by itself.
